nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SERPINF2 (chromosome 17p13) are the initiating lesion. The best-characterised alleles are in-frame deletions and frameshifts that produce a misfolded protein retained in the endoplasmic reticulum: alpha-2-PI Okinawa (deletion of Glu137) and alpha-2-PI Nara, together with a single-thymine deletion in exon 5 that truncates the protein after 83 native residues. Most variants therefore cause a quantitative (type I) deficiency with parallel loss of antigen and activity. Heterozygous carriers of a single pathogenic allele, such as the reactive-site-adjacent missense p.Val384Met or the intron 6 splice-donor allele Artas that skips exon 6, have intermediate activity and antigen and bleed after surgery or trauma. Variants are largely private to individual families.

nodes.description: Without alpha-2-antiplasmin, plasmin generated on the fibrin surface is neither neutralised in a covalent serpin complex nor prevented from binding fibrin, and no inhibitor is cross-linked into the clot by factor XIIIa. Fibrin-bound plasmin therefore degrades the clot freely. Plasma fibrinogen stays normal, consistent with alpha-2-macroglobulin still restraining free plasmin in the circulation.
